gap: Whether the Diabetes dataset's Outcome column is part of the feature matrix.
chosen: Use only the 8 listed features; Outcome excluded.
rationale: Table I reports the 8 features; anomaly detection is unsupervised and Outcome is a label.
quote: First, for the Diabetes dataset [1] consider a scenario in which selected features are assigned greater sensitivity.

rationale: No preprocessing is stated, and A3/A5 diagonal values are described as feature sensitivities in original feature units.

gap: T-test variant (Student vs Welch), sidedness, and equal-variance assumption.
chosen: two-sided Student t-test with equal variances (Python scipy.stats.ttest_ind default).
rationale: The paper says only 't-test for independent samples'; the implementation is Python and does not mention Welch.
quote: We compare the mean values of the features of the anomalies identified by the EIF and AIF(A3) using a t-test for independent samples.

gap: Random seeds and number of repeated runs for forests and p-values.
chosen: One fixed seed per model and a single run; no averaging.
rationale: Table I gives one value per cell with no spread; authors do not report repetitions.

gap: Exact size and tie handling for 'top 10%' anomaly sets.
chosen: Take the 77 highest anomaly scores (ceil), breaking ties by stable rank.
quote: For each model, we mark as anomalies the data points whose anomaly scores fall within the top 10% of all scores produced by that model.

gap: Extension level used for the Diabetes EIF/AIF forests.
rationale: Section II-D discusses extension levels but the Diabetes experiment does not state one; full extension matches the arbitrary-orientation description.
quote: In the fully extended case (d −1 extensions), the hyperplanes may take arbitrary orientations in the d-dimensional feature space

gap: How the random intercept point p is drawn.
options: uniformly in the bounding box of current X
sample one existing point from X
chosen: Uniformly in the bounding box of the current X, coordinate-wise.
rationale: Algorithm 2 says 'within the range of X' but not whether from data or box; EIF convention uses uniform intercept.
quote: Randomly select an intercept point p ∈Rdim{X} within the range of X.

gap: Mapping of diagonal entries of A to dataset columns.
options: Table I order Age, DPF, Pregnancies, ...
chosen: Table I order: Age and DPF are coordinates 1 and 2.
rationale: A3/A4/A5 put the manipulated entries first, and the text says those entries are Age and DPF.
quote: so that the features age and DPF are assigned greater sensitivity

gap: Independence of EIF and AIF anomaly sets in the t-test when observations overlap.
options: Use paired test on overlapping observations
chosen: Treat groups as independent and ignore overlap.
rationale: The paper explicitly says independent samples; no paired analysis is described.
quote: using a t-test for independent samples

gap: Handling zero values in Glucose, BloodPressure, SkinThickness, Insulin, BMI.
rationale: No missing-value handling is stated; Kaggle version contains zeros but paper reports no filtering.

options: Try to reproduce exact unrounded p
chosen: Match printed value to two decimals; treat 0.01 as the displayed rounded p-value.
rationale: Table I prints two decimals; no exact unrounded p-values are given.
quote: The resulting p-values are reported in the first column of Table I.

gap: Whether EIF and AIF use identical random subsamples/intercepts for fair comparison.
chosen: Common random seed for data subsampling where possible, independent normal-vector draws per model.
rationale: Not stated; common subsamples reduce variance but AIF normal draws must differ.
